full_judgment:
2. Facts leading to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that the petitioner herein as pre-emptor instituted Miscellaneous Case No.4 of 2005 before the Assistant Judge, Second Court, Dhaka for pre-emption of the case gland. On transfer to the fourth Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Dhaka, the case was re-numbered as Miscellaneous No.1116 of 2008. The pre-emptor contended, inter alia, that out of 1.32 acres land of the C.S. Plot No.17, an area of 88 decimals of land belonged to M. Bazlur Rahman Khan alias Gutu Mia and Khorsheduzzaman, and their names have been recorded in S.A. Khatian No.7. Mohammad Bazlur Rahman Khan by registered’ Kabala No.11743 dated 16.11.1957 sold 44 decimals of land to Abdul Barek, the father of the pre-emptor and delivered possession thereof. Khorsheduzzaman also sold 44 decimals of land by registered Kabala No.13240 dated 17.12.1957 to Abdul Barek, the father of the pre-emptor and delivered possession thereof. Abdul Barek died leaving behind his wife Nurbanu, 6 sons, namely Abdul Mailman, Abdul Latif, Showkat Akbar, M.A. Majid, the petitioner Hazrat Ali, Minnot Ali and one daughter, namely Hazera Khatun. Thereafter, Nurbanu died leaving behind six sons and one daughter. Showkat Akbar died leaving behind two wives namely, Shamima Akhter, the opposite party No.6 and Parveen Akhter, the opposite party No.12 and three sons and four daughters, the opposite party Nos.7- 11, 13 and 14. Hazera Begum, daughter of Late Abdul Barek died leaving behind her husband, four sons and two daughters who are the opposite party Nos.15- 21 of this application. The S.A. recorded owner Khorsheduzzaman died leaving behind one son, namely Moniruzzaman. Other S.A. recorded owner Bazlur Rahman Khan died leaving behind his one son, namely Enamul Haque. The name of the opposite party No.24 was recorded in R.S. Khatian No.14 and hence, she was made party in the case. In this way, the pre-emptor is a co-sharer by inheritance in respect of the case holding. The pre-emptor recently came to know from the locality that the opposite party No.7, Abdul Latif had sold out some of the properties from different plots to the pre-emptees and thereafter; on 18.12.2004, the pre-emptor upon obtaining the certified copy of the Kabala deed No.17673 dated 06.12.2004 came to know that the opposite party No.7 had sold out the case property to the pre-emptee Nos.1-6 of this pre- emption miscellaneous case. The pre-emptee Nos.1-6 are strangers to the case land and the vendor, opposite party No.7 did not serve any notice upon the pre-emptor of this pre-emption case. Hence, the pre-emptor filed this case. 

 3. The pre-emptee Nos. 1-6 contested the case by filling written objection. They contended that the case is not maintainable in its present form. The case is barred by the principle of waiver, acquiescence and estoppels; barred by limitation and bad for defect of party. It is also contended that late Abdul Barek, the father of the vendor Abdul Latif was the recorded tenant of R.S. Khatian No. 14. Abdul Barek died leaving behind 6 sons including Abdul Latif, the vendor opposite party No.7 and one daughter and his wife. The pre-emptor is a powerful man of the locality and there exists a good relation between the pre-emptor and pre-emptee No.l. As the vendor opposite party No.7 is the full brother of the pre- emptor, the pre-emptor offered pre-emptee No.1 to purchase the case land of the vendor opposite party No.7. The pre-emptees are living in London for quite a long time and they occasionally come to Bangladesh. The Pre-emptor being the brother of the vendor proposed to pre-emptee No. 1 to purchase the land, but the pre-emptees, at first, did not show any interest for purchasing the land. But, due to the persuasion of the pre-emptor and his brother, the vendor, the pre-emptees agreed to purchase the land. The vendor Abdul Latif by taking Tk.50,000/- from pre-emptee Nos.1-6 had delivered possession of the case land to pre-emtee Nos. 1-6 on 07.09.2004 and thereafter, in presence of respectable people of the locality, 19.11.2004, a Civil Engineer by drawing map fixed the boundary of the plot and again on 03.12.2004, another Civil Engineer prepared a map of the plot and had constructed a pucca boundary wall. In this connection, the pre-emptee Nos.1-6 had spent a sum of Tk. 4,00,000/=. The pre-emptor was present along with others on 07.12.2004 when the vendor, Abdul Latif by registered Kabala No.17673 sold out the case property to pre-emptee Nos. 1- 6. The pre-emptees mutated the case land in their names. By spending Tk.10,00,000/=, the pre-emptees filled the case land with earth and also constructed a semipucca house on the said land and also brought electric and gas connection thereto and also let out the said house to different tenants. The pre- emptee Nos.1-6 are not strangers in the case land. In the vicinity, on the western side of the case land, the pre-emptee No.1 had also purchased 4 kathas of land vide sale deed No.17004 dated 22.11.1994 which is within the case Khatian. The pre-emptee No. | had also constructed a two storitAd building on the said 4 kathas of land, and, as such, the pre-emptees are co-sharers of the land in question. The pre-emptor is a very powerful man of the said locality and nobody purchase any land without the consent of the pre-emptor. The pre-emptor in order to harass the pre- emptees filed the case. The instant pre- emption case is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 4. The vendor Abdul Latif filed written objection stating that the instant pre-emption miscellaneous case is not maintainable in its present form. The case is barred by limitation. There is no cause for filing this application. The further case of the vendor Abdul Latif (the opposite party No.7) is that on 02.08.2004, he proposed to the pre-emptor M. A. Majid and others for purchasing the case land, which all of them refused. Pre-emptee Nos.1-6 are not strangers in the case land and in the vicinity, on the western side of the case land, pre-emptee No.1 had also purchased 4 kathas of land vide sale deed No.17004 dated 22.11.1994, which is within the case Khatian. Pre-emptee No.1 had also constructed a two storied building on the said 4 Kathas of land and as such, the pre-emptees are co-sharers of the land in question. The pre-emptor’s brothers had sold out land to different persons by different kabalas including to the pre-emptee Nos.1-6 and others. On the basis of two deeds, the pre-emptee Nos. 1-6 had been possessing and enjoying 6¼ kathas of land in the case plot, and as such, the instant pre-emption is liable to be dismissed.
